synth.critique:
Today's west wing (draft L) is 0-24 x 13-54, 984 sf gross, of which the server room uses 57 sf. It has the area for two good guest suites, but the space is in the wrong places.
- Bedroom 2 is 24'0" x 13'10" (331 sf) plus a 19 sf alcove that does nothing. It has one window on the back wall, and its terrace-side wall is blank.
- WIC 2 is 6'5" x 4'2" (about 27 sf, about 6 lf of hanging). That is a reach-in, not a walk-in.
- Bath 2 is 13'0" x 7'7" (99 sf). It has one sink, and the door at x 7-9.5 looks straight at the toilet.
- The hall is an L of about 60 sf, about 3'0" clear, with no daylight and an 11 ft dog-leg. It opens off a 3'5" living-room opening with no door, so great-room noise reaches every bedroom door.
- Bedroom 3 is 17'6" x 12'4" (215 sf, Michael's option A). It has one 5 ft window and shares an 8'8" bare stud wall with the server room, which is the main noise risk.
- Bath 3 is 11'5" x 7'4" (83 sf). Its shower is drawn 26" wide, under the IRC 30" minimum. That is the worst defect in the wing. It has a single 4 ft vanity.
- Melissa's bedroom 3 sequence works: a 4'4" vestibule leads to the bath and to Closet 3 (8'4" x 7'4", 61 sf, which also buffers the living room and lounge).

Neither suite meets the high-end targets for closet, vanity, toilet privacy, hall or sound. Bedroom 2's extra width and the dark hall are the space to rebalance, so no addition is required.

Expansion room: only the west wall (x 0 to x -4) can move cleanly. The back wall would come within about 5 ft of the swim water and would take terrace. A full-length west push keeps the hip roof a plain rectangle.

synth.why:
G1 brings both rooms up to real guest suites without adding square footage or touching the roof.
- It fixes the most serious problem: bath 3's 26" shower, which is under code.
- It replaces the dark 3 ft dog-leg hall with a daylit 6 ft foyer that is a few steps from the living room.
- Suite 2 gets a real walk-in closet and a second window wall.
- Both baths get 60" vanities, with the toilet out of the door sightline.
- The server wall is properly sound-isolated.
- It keeps almost everything Melissa drew, plus Michael's option A bedroom and his linen closet.

W4 is the upgrade path if the budget and the west setback allow. It meets every target in both suites, but it costs roughly $35-55k, raises the ridge and asks Melissa to give up toilets beside the sinks. V1 makes one excellent suite but leaves bedroom 3 secondary.

decisions.q: Is it OK that bath 2 is reached through the walk-in closet instead of straight from the bedroom?
decisions.rec: Yes. It frees bedroom 2's wall and gives the suite a real closet. A direct bedroom door can be added at x 7-9.5 if guests find the walk-through awkward.

decisions.q: Should a solid-core sealed door go in the 3'5" living-room opening, so the guest wing can be closed off during parties?
decisions.rec: Yes. Hinge it at y 37.9 so it swings into the foyer. It blocks great-room noise and the sightline into bedroom 3.

decisions.q: Should the server room get its own quiet ductless mini-split and a sealed solid-core door?
decisions.rec: Yes. Put the condenser on the west side, and surface-mount the panels so the bedroom 3 sound wall stays intact.

decisions.q: Melissa: can bedroom 3's door move from the hall to the new foyer wall?
decisions.rec: Yes. Everything else in her suite 3 (vestibule, closet, outside-corner bath, full-depth shower) stays as she drew it.

decisions.q: Melissa: in bath 3, can the toilet move to the door wall so a 60" vanity and a full 36" shower fit?
decisions.rec: Yes. Today's 26" shower fails code, and this is the simplest fix.

decisions.q: Is the linen as a 22" deep foyer cabinet enough, in place of the old linen nook?
decisions.rec: Yes. It keeps the linen storage Michael approved, right at the suite doors.

decisions.q: Should we price and check the survey for the 4 ft west push (option W4) as a later upgrade?
decisions.rec: Build G1 now. Check the west setback before committing, since W4 is about $35-55k and raises the wing ridge by 1'4".

decisions.q: Should there be a tub anywhere in the guest wing?
decisions.rec: No. Walk-in showers suit guests better. If a tub is wanted, it only fits in W4's bath 2.

I measured today's west wing in draft L (plan-generator.py, x 0-24, y 13-54, about 984 sf). It has the bones of two suites but misses most of the high-end targets.

- Bedroom 2 (0-24 x 13-26.8) is 24'0" x 13'10" (331 sf), plus a 4'7" x 4'2" door alcove. That is larger than most primary bedrooms. It has only one window, 9 ft wide on the back (pond) wall at x 10.5-19.5, and a blank side wall.
- WIC 2 (13-19.4 x 26.8-31) is 6'5" x 4'2", about 27 sf. That is a reach-in, not a walk-in (the target is 40-60 sf).
- Bath 2 (0-13 x 26.8-34.4) is 13'0" x 7'7" (99 sf). It has a 3'5" x 7'2" tub/shower on the outside wall, one sink in a 5'5" vanity, and an open toilet beside the sink.
- The hall (13-24 x 31-34.4) is 11'0" x 3'5" on centers, about 3'0"-3'1" clear. The passage (17.5-24 x 34.4-38) is 6'6" x 3'7". Neither has daylight. The opening from the living room is 3'5".
- Bedroom 3 (0-17.5 x 34.4-46.7) is 17'6" x 12'4" (216 sf), the option A size Michael chose. It has windows on one wall only (x 0, 5 ft). Its right wall at x 17.5 is shared for 8'8" with the server room.
- Bath 3 (0-11.4 x 46.7-54) is 11'5" x 7'4" (83 sf). The shower is drawn 2'2" (26") wide, which is under the 30" code minimum and well under a real 36" x 60" shower. It has one 4 ft vanity, and the toilet sits beside the sink.
- The vestibule (4'4") and Closet 3 (8'4" x 7'4", 61 sf) work and meet the target.
- The server room (6'6" x 8'8") opens right at the living-room passage and shares a bare stud wall with bedroom 3. Of everything in the wing, it is the worst noise source next to a bedroom.

Score against the targets:
- Bedroom size: pass for both.
- Walk-in closet: fail for suite 2, pass for suite 3.
- 60" vanity or two sinks: fail for both.
- Toilet out of view: fail for both.
- Real shower: suite 2 has a tub/shower; suite 3 fails code.
- Windows on two walls: fail for both.
- 42" hall with daylight: fail.
- Short walk from the living room: pass, about 10-12 ft.
- Sound separation: weak.

Site limits for expanding:
- West (x < 0): open lawn. The water is more than 7 ft past y 0 there.
- Back (y < 13): the pond's swim edge is at y 4.38 at x 24, y 3.4 at x 20 and y 0.6 at x 14. A back wall at y 9.5 therefore keeps at least 5.1 ft to the water. The terrace polygon covers x 14-24 behind the wing (about y 1-13). A back push takes a 10 x 3.5 ft corner of it (35 sf) and leaves a 5-8 ft terrace walk behind the wing.
- Roof: a hip held at 8:12 stays clean if the wing stays a plain rectangle, so either push must run the full width or the full length. A partial bump would add a hip and valley.

Two options follow. Both keep the server room, the lounge, the living room, the x 24 opening and the server door at y 38 exactly where they are. Both keep these walls: y 34.4 (bedroom 3), y 46.7, x 17.5 at the server and y 54. Both widen the hall to 4'0" on centers (about 3'7" clear) with a skylight or solar tube at about (15.5, 32.4). Option A (west 4 ft, +164 sf) is my recommendation: it makes both suites hit the targets. Option B (back 3.5 ft, +84 sf) is the cheaper roof change: the same hip slides back, as in the primary-bath study. It mainly upgrades suite 2.

These upgrades apply to either option:
- Server room: double or staggered studs with mineral wool on its x 17.5 and y 38 walls, plus a solid-core gasketed door. It keeps its own mini-split, with the condenser outside on the west side.
- Bedroom 3: a 2 ft built-in wardrobe and TV wall on the server side as a second buffer.

PROBLEMS
1. Code: Bath 3 is not "unchanged" as the proposal says. Draft L has a 26" shower (0.4-2.6), which is under the 30" minimum, the toilet at x 5 and a 4 ft vanity at 7.2-11.2. The proposal redraws it with the shower 0.4-3.6, the vanity 4.2-8.7 and the toilet 9.1-10.7. That puts the toilet centerline (9.9) only 14.4" from the vanity end (8.7), under the IRC 15" minimum.

A 3.4 ft pocket would run either into y 31.1-34.5, where the new glass panel (31.3-33.7) is, or into y 37.9-41.3. That second wall is the server room's east wall, and the living-room media built-in (24.25-25.8 x 39-54.7) is fastened to it. A pocket door also seals poorly, which defeats the reason for adding it.
